breadcrumbs.current: History of Neolithic Age or New Stone Age

hero.title: Neolithic Age: The Food-Producing Revolution
hero.description: The Neolithic Age marks the profound transition from nomadic hunter-gatherer societies to sedentary, agriculture-based civilizations.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The Neolithic transition in India occurred at different times across various regions.

cards.details: Earliest evidence of farming at Mehrgarh (Balochistan), focusing on wheat and barley cultivation.
Widespread diffusion of agricultural communities across the Indus plains and Kashmir valley (Burzahom).
The transition into Chalcolithic phases; increased use of copper alongside stone tools.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Remember the key Neolithic sites using 'B.M.P.C'.

items.title: B.M.P.C
items.decryption: B (Burzahom-Pit dwellings), M (Mehrgarh-Oldest farming), P (Piklihal-Cattle herding), C (Chirand-Bone tools).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming Neolithic Age was pan-Indian simultaneously; it evolved at different times in different regions.
Thinking copper was absent in all Neolithic sites; late Neolithic stages overlap with Chalcolithic transition.
Confusing pit dwellings (Burzahom) as a pan-Indian feature; they were specific to cold regions.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Master the Neolithic Revolution, technological advances in stone and pottery, regional cultures, dwelling habits, and South Indian ash mounds.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Mehrgarh: Balochistan
  • Burzahom: Kashmir
  • Chirand: Bihar
  • Piklihal/Utnur: South India

Cultural Traits

  • Agriculture (Wheat/Barley/Rice)
  • Domestication of animals
  • Polished stone tools
  • Pottery development
  • Technological Shifts:
    • Ground and polished stone celts.
    • Bone tools (evident in Chirand).
    • Hand-made pottery (followed by wheel-made).
SiteSignificant Feature
MehrgarhOldest Neolithic site; pre-pottery.
BurzahomPit dwellings, burial of dogs with humans.
ChirandUse of bone implements.
UtnurCattle penning/Ash mounds.

flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Hover or click to flip the card and test your retention of key Neolithic facts.

cards.back: V. Gordon Childe, in his 1936 book Man Makes Himself, to describe the shift from food-gathering to food-producing.

cards.front: What unique feature defines the dwellings of Burzahom and Gufkral?
cards.back: Pit-dwellings. Circular or oval subterranean pits dug into the loessic tablelands (Karewas) with mud-plastered walls.

cards.front: Which Indian site yields the earliest evidence of agriculture?
cards.back: Lahuradewa in UP for rice (c. 9000-8000 BCE) and Mehrgarh in Balochistan for wheat/barley (c. 7000 BCE).

cards.front: What are South Indian ash mounds composed of?
cards.back: Vitrified and accumulated burnt cow dung from Neolithic cattle enclosures (sites: Kupgal, Utnur, Piklihal).

cards.front: Which Neolithic site is famous for a large number of bone tools?
cards.back: Chirand in Bihar. It yielded a dense assemblage of bone tools, primarily chisels and scrapers made of deer antlers.

cards.front: What is the typical tool of the Neolithic period?
cards.back: The Celt, which is a ground and polished stone axe used for clearing forests and wood-working.

mockIntro.title: UPSC Civil Services Prelims Mock Test
mockIntro.description: Contains 10 multi-statement questions testing conceptual understanding and site identification. 1/3 negative marking applies.
rules: Each incorrect answer deducts 0.66 marks (1/3rd penalty).
Questions match the current UPSC Prelims standards (multi-statement and matching pairs).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sites are classified as Kashmir Neolithic? (Select all that apply)
practiceQuestions.sol: Burzahom and Gufkral are Kashmir Neolithic; Mehrgarh is in Balochistan, Sarutaru is in Assam.

practiceQuestions.q: The earliest agricultural site Mehrgarh is located on the bank of which river pass basin?

mockTestQuestions.q:
With reference to the Southern Neolithic ash mounds, consider the following statements:
1. They are composed of vitrified cow dung deposits.
2. Utnur and Kupgal are famous ash mound sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Southern Neolithic ash mounds represent burnt cow dung accumulations from cattle pens.
